h1: The 6 Best Simple Cell Phones for Seniors With Big Buttons and SOS Keys, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Simple Cell Phones for Seniors: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 simple cell phones for seniors, big button and flip, compared on SOS key, VoLTE, unlocked 4G, dock charging and ease of use.
summary: The artfone A400 is the best simple phone for most seniors, with big buttons, an SOS button, large fonts, a three-slot charging dock and unlocked 4G. The Easyfone Prime-A6 is the strong alternative, the Prime-T6 uses picture buttons for caregivers, and the Lively Jitterbug Flip2 adds a paid urgent response service.
intro: The word simple hides three different things on a phone: big physical buttons, a small menu and a short list of features. A phone can have giant keys and still bury the volume setting four screens deep. The best simple phones make the common jobs one press, calling a family member, answering and finding the SOS key in the dark, and leave everything else out.

We ranked six simple phones, mostly big-button candy bars plus one flip, with attention to SOS keys, VoLTE and unlocked 4G, and how each charges. Our group has a duplicate listing of the Easyfone Prime-A6 that we merged. Confirm that a phone works on your carrier before buying, since 4G unlocked phones vary in network support.

products.name: artfone A400 Big Button Cell Phone for Seniors, 4G LTE Unlocked, Silver
products.verdict: Big buttons, an SOS button, large fonts, voice time and a three-slot charging dock, unlocked.
products.description:
The artfone A400 is a big-button phone with a 4G LTE unlocked radio, an SOS button, large fonts, voice time announcement and a charging dock with three slots. It costs $50 to $100.

It wins because it solves the daily frustrations: a dock means the phone is dropped into a cradle instead of fumbling with a cable, large fonts help weak eyesight, and unlocked 4G lets the family keep their carrier. The SOS button calls saved numbers in an emergency. The three-slot dock also charges spare batteries.

Buy it for a first phone for an older relative. Test the signal where they live.
products.idealFor: A first phone for an older relative.
products.skipIf: You want a monitored response service.

products.name: Easyfone Prime-A6 Unlocked 4G Big Button Cell Phone for Seniors, Black
products.verdict: Big buttons, a dedicated SOS emergency feature and an ultra-simple interface, unlocked 4G.
products.description:
The Easyfone Prime-A6 is a big-button unlocked 4G phone with an SOS emergency feature and an ultra-simple interface. Price is $50 to $100.

Second place follows since it matches the artfone on the essentials, with a very uncluttered menu. It lacks the charging dock and the voice time feature, so charging needs a cable.

Buy it for the simplest menu. Choose the artfone for the dock.
products.idealFor: Users who want the simplest menu.

products.name: Easyfone Prime-T6 4G Picture Button Cell Phone for Seniors
products.verdict: Picture buttons for one-touch dialing, an SOS button and a charging dock.
products.description:
The Easyfone Prime-T6 is a 4G phone with picture buttons, an SOS button and a charging dock. It costs $50 to $100.

Picture buttons hold a photo of each contact, so a user presses a face rather than reading a name. That helps people with memory difficulty. It ranks third because only a few contacts fit.

Buy it for caregivers who want picture-first dialing. Not for anyone who needs many contacts.

products.name: LIVELY Jitterbug Flip Cell Phone for Seniors, Flip2, Graphite
products.verdict: A classic flip with an Urgent Response button, which requires Lively service.
products.description:
The Jitterbug Flip2 is a classic flip phone with an Urgent Response button and a requirement for Lively service. The handset costs $25 to $50.

The urgent response button connects to a live service, which is the main reason families choose it. It ranks fourth because it requires a service plan and cannot use another carrier.

Buy it for an established emergency service. Skip it to keep your own carrier.
products.idealFor: Families wanting a monitored response service.
products.skipIf: You want to keep your carrier.

products.name: artfone A400 4G VoLTE Big Button Cell Phone Unlocked for Seniors, Silver
products.verdict: A VoLTE big-button phone with an SOS button and a 2MP camera for $25 to $50.
products.description:
This artfone A400 listing names VoLTE support, an SOS button and a 2MP camera, and the phone is unlocked. It costs $25 to $50.

VoLTE matters because US carriers have shut down older networks, and a phone without VoLTE may not make calls. It ranks fifth because it lists no dock or large fonts.

Buy it for confirmed VoLTE at a low price. Check carrier support.

products.name: artfone C1+4G Cell Phone for Seniors, Large Buttons Basic Phone, Black
products.verdict: A large-button basic phone with SOS, FM radio, voice time and speed dial.
products.description:
The artfone C1+4G is a basic phone with large buttons, an SOS button, FM radio, voice time and speed dial. It costs $25 to $50.

FM radio is a nice bonus for company. It ranks last because the listing gives no dock and less detail on network support.

Buy it for basic simplicity at a low price. Verify the 4G bands.

whatMatters.detail: Carriers run voice over LTE now, and a phone without VoLTE may not call. Check the listing and your carrier's compatibility list.
An SOS key calls saved numbers in an emergency. A monitored service adds a live operator but costs a subscription.
Big raised keys and large fonts help stiff fingers and weak eyesight. Check font size and brightness.
A dock avoids small cable plugs. It also gives a visible home for the phone.
Add monthly plan costs to the handset price over a year.

howToChoose.intro: Pick the need first, then check the network.

cards.label: Unlocked
cards.text: Use any compatible carrier. The artfone and Easyfone phones are unlocked.

cards.label: Service plan
cards.text: Lively bundles the phone with a response service. The Jitterbug requires it.

howToChoose.note: Choose unlocked to control cost, and a service plan for a monitored button.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Picture buttons, few features and one-press calling. Add family numbers before handing over.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Easyfone Prime-T6 is the best fit. This is not medical advice.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a dock and large fonts. The artfone A400 at $50 to $100 has both.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Calls are occasional. The artfone C1+4G at $25 to $50 is enough.

faq.q: Will these work on my carrier?
faq.a: Unlocked 4G phones work on compatible bands. Check your carrier's tool with the model.
Skipping VoLTE. Without it, calls may fail. Confirm support.
If you want a live emergency service, yes. Otherwise an unlocked phone costs less.

faq.q: How do I set up speed dial?
faq.a: Save contacts, then assign them to number keys per the manual. Test each key.

faq.q: How do I set the SOS key?
faq.a: Enter emergency numbers in settings and test the alert. Tell contacts to expect it.

faq.q: Do they have hearing aid support?
faq.a: The listings do not say. Check the maker for a hearing aid rating.

finalTake: The artfone A400 is the best simple phone for most seniors, with big buttons, SOS and a charging dock. The Easyfone Prime-A6 has the simplest menu, the Prime-T6 helps picture dialing, and the Jitterbug Flip2 is for those wanting a monitored service.
